record_type_quote:
The original study uses the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (NSHAP). The data used
in the replication is from a different source that contains similar variables: the Midlife in the United
States (MIDUS Refresher).

targets.title: Past-Year Sexual Inactivity Among Older Married Persons and Their Partners.
targets.evidence_quote:
Despite this difference, as in the original study, logistic
regressions are employed; and it is possible to evaluate how marital duration and age impact sexual
inactivity among older married people, which corresponds to the research claims of interest for the
replication.
targets.outcome_quote:
Result: Marital duration is positively associated with sexual inactivity (b = 0.04, SE b = 0.03, OR =
1.04). The effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level (p = 0.309), two-tailed test.
Consequently, this claim was not replicated.
targets.outcome_reasoning:
Three marital-duration claims are explicitly judged not replicated, while both age claims are explicitly judged replicated. The supporting age passage reads: Result: Age is positively associated with sexual inactivity (b = 0.11, SE b = 0.02, OR = 1.11). The
effect is statistically significant at the 5% level (p = 0.000), two-tailed test. Consequently, this
claim was replicated.
